# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers say the schedule and no-show subs are what push the log down the list, so one group named plainly for that is how a superintendent would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk answer on this line; both answers are on topic about why other work came first.

founder.order_why: The flow runs in a sensible order: name, market, context, how often the end-of-day log happens, what else is hard, how supers keep the record today, then who runs the interviews.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same kicker and the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'), so the context screen seems to come back after the recall-window question on screen 4.
founder.missing: For Fresco, the flow never asks who pays or what they would pay: the general contractor pays about $1k per site per month (less on multi-site or multi-month terms), and the buyer is not the superintendent. It also never asks for the solution (narrated site-walk videos turned into notes, texted to the crew and pushed to Procore/ACC), so the study can't test the solution, the price or the contractor's buying steps.

PRIMARY.order_why: Asking which part of my day I'd most like made easier comes before the question about how my last photo upload went, so I'm picking a pain point before I've been walked back through the log I actually wrote.
PRIMARY.missing: How long the daily log took me, and when I wrote it (end of day or that night). Where the photos came from, since I take them on my phone all day and then spend hours getting them into Procore. Whether I've had to pull old logs and photos to back up a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.why5: It still says what I typed, US with no region, and the kicker names the product as I describe it.

screens.why5: Nothing of the founder's product or roles leaks, and my pick of 'Read and tap' is kept as I chose it.

screens.why1: Once I've picked how superintendents answer, the next obvious step is deciding who gets the link, and this is the last screen before sending.
screens.why2: The three choices are plain to me as a founder: supers I know by name, a list from Keel's search, or one open link posted where supers already gather.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm sending to supers I've met on site visits around the Bay Area or posting in a group, so I can answer this from my own situation.
screens.why4: Named people, a Keel-found list and an open group link are distinct and cover how I'd reach superintendents, and my pick (supers by name) is there.
screens.why5: Nothing here changes what I typed about superintendents and the daily log, and it's a founder-only screen, so nothing reaches a respondent.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits under the title with its deciding number ('Frequency: 4 counted'), and the Frequency card shows the bar of 5 needed; naming only Frequency is odd, though, when Importance and Current solution are also stuck at 4 counted.
screens.why_b2: The tally reads at a glance as 4 beliefs, 1 holding and 3 too few to call over 7 people, and each card puts its count beside its bar (6 of 7 at the bar; 4 counted against 5 needed).
screens.why_b3: All four beliefs are the lines I checked on the way in, word for word, under the names Prevalence, Frequency, Importance and Current solution.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need more counted answers, but the page never says to send the study to more superintendents, nor why 3 of my 7 weren't counted on three cards.
screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, three beliefs are honestly called too few to call, and Prevalence at exactly 6 of 7 is marked 'at the bar' rather than strong; only my own pitch under the title could read like a finding.
screens.instead: Too few to call: Frequency, Importance and Current solution each have 4 of 7 counted, one short of the 5 needed (3 weren't counted because ...). Send the study to more superintendents to decide them. Prevalence holds, just, at 6 of 7.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Holding up' sits right beside its deciding number, '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I know it held and by exactly how much.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows seven cells, six for and one against, on an axis from 0 to 7 with the marker at 6 labelled 'at least 8 in 10', so what is counted, over how many, and where the bar sits are plain at first look.
screens.why_b3: The card is titled Prevalence, and 'At least 8 in 10 construction superintendents wrote their daily log in the trailer in the last 5 working days' is my band, my people and my window, put in the gate's own words about the trailer I described.
screens.why_b4: 'Common among these 7, at your bar exactly' plus a pointer to the next two cards tells me to keep reading, but not what an exactly-at-the-bar result means for Fresco or what I should check before leaning on it.
screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, the count line says 'a small group: a lean, not a call', and 'at the bar' / 'at your bar exactly' stop the result from being called strong; the 'the most recent time it happened' tag on a yes/no gate is odd but claims nothing beyond the answers.
screens.instead: Common among these 7, but exactly at your bar: one more No would have put it below, so treat this as a lean and see whether How often and the importance card back it up before you lean on it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both.
screens.why_b2: The axis (working days out of 5) and the 4 counted are plain, but 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 and all 4 cells for me reads at first like I'm already at the bar. The 0 tick and a 'short of it' legend with nobody short of it also took a second look.
screens.why_b3: Frequency is the name I checked, and 'write their daily log in the trailer on 4 to 5 working days out of 5' is my trailer, my daily log and my range, in my words.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that all four counted supers sit inside my range with a middle answer of 5, or that one more countable answer would decide it.
screens.why_b5: The n and 'a small group' are said honestly. But the question is tagged '— the most recent time it happened' when it asks for a count over the last 5 working days, and the bar line reads like a hit when the card can't call it.
screens.instead: Too few to call: all 4 supers counted log in the trailer 4 or 5 days of 5 (middle answer 5), but 5 are needed. One more countable answer settles it, so it is leaning your way, not proven.

screens.why_b1: The status Too few to call sits right beside the deciding number, 4 counted with 5 needed, and the So line repeats both.
screens.why_b2: Bars counting 8 picks from 4 people read plainly, but the strip's bar marked as 4 of 5 took me a second look to see it means 4 of the 5 needed have to put my item in their two.
screens.why_b3: Both the name Importance and the belief line are the ones I checked, and my own row keeps my words, Logging the day's photos and notes.
screens.why_b4: Nothing is settled here yet is generic: it does not tell me to get one more superintendent counted, or that 2 for and 2 against means I already need 3 of the next 1 to hold, which I cannot get.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible at 6 answered and 4 counted, the two not counted are named with reasons, and the small group is called a lean, not a call, with no overstatement.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put the log in their two, and schedule and subs drew 3 picks each; get one more superintendent counted, though even a yes leaves 3 of 5, below the 4 you need.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there's no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The rung counts and 'your line · below here, today's way fell short' read at once, but the strip's '4 of 5' with its marker at 4 and a ghost cell took me a second look to see it means four counted against a floor of five, not four of five people for me.
screens.why_b3: The title and the belief line are the ones I checked word for word, and the bar names my own rung 'Done in the trailer in under an hour'.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that one more counted answer would decide it, or that 3 of the 4 counted already fell short.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, the low n is said ('a small group: a lean, not a call'), and nothing is claimed beyond the four counted, though the question asked about uploading photos while the answers grade the whole log.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted fell short of 'Done in the trailer in under an hour' (2 in 3 needed), but 5 must be counted; one more superintendent's answer settles it. Ask about the log, not just the photo upload, next time.

screens.why_b1: Too few to call is stated with 4 counted, 5 needed beside it, but the box never says how the 4 split, so I see 2 against and cannot tell if the other 2 put the log in their two.
screens.why_b3: Importance and the belief line are word for word what I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: Too few to call implies get more superintendents to answer, but nothing says how many more or what the schedule-and-subs theme means for pitching the log as a top pain.
screens.why_b5: The n is visible, the call is withheld at 4 of 5, and the theme is shown as 2 people, not as what supers think.
screens.why_b6: Two supers who put schedule and no-show subs above the log, one done on the tablet before the gate and one who lets the log wait till morning, tell me the log is deferrable, which I did not type.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put the log in their two, 2 put schedule and subs first; you need 1 more answer, and both against say the log can wait while the schedule cannot.

screens.why1: As the opener, it makes sense to check that my jobs run on Procore or ACC before asking me about getting photos and notes into the daily log there.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms every super I know logs on, so I'd answer this on the first read or hearing.
screens.why3: I know exactly which platform each of my jobs runs on because I'm in it every day.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it completely, and a screener needs no escape; 'any of the jobs' handles a super split across two platforms.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's Procore-or-ACC condition, and nothing about a product or a scribe reaches me.
screens.why6: The question says well and 'ACC' is said on site, but 'I'll read 2 options. Yes; or No.' is stiff for a yes/no; the screener should just end with 'Yes or no.'

screens.why1: Right after confirming my jobs run on Procore or ACC, asking whether I did my daily log in the last week is the obvious next step before asking how it went.
screens.why2: Daily log and trailer are my everyday words, and I can answer it on one read.
screens.why3: I know exactly where and when I wrote my logs this past week.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it for a gate, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to this question.
screens.why5: The problem was typing the log up after the walks instead of on them; 'in the trailer' turns that into a place, so a night at the kitchen table doesn't count.
screens.why6: Short, one question, 'Yes or no' at the end; easy to answer on one hearing.
screens.why7: Both answers are possible, but 'in the trailer' bends the stem off the founder's event: a super who typed it up at home after the walks truly had the problem and still says No, and most of us write it in the trailer anyway, so Yes leans toward the circumstance.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to writing my log in the trailer, asking how many of the last five days I did it is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log and trailer are my words, but 'in the trailer' makes me stop: some nights I finish it in the truck or at the kitchen table, and I'm not sure whether those days count.
screens.why3: I know which days this week I sat down and did the log, so I can answer from my own week.
screens.why4: One button per working day from 1 to 5 with 'I can't recall' apart covers every answer I could give, and none overlap.
screens.why5: Nothing about a product leaks, but the problem is getting the walk's photos and notes into the log once the walks are done, and pinning it to the trailer drifts from that onto where I sit.
screens.why6: Short, one question, and 'a number from 1 to 5, or say you can't recall' is easy to hold and answer by ear.
screens.why7: The measure (days of the window), the shape (1 to 5, unit said once) and the escape all meet the card, but the event packs a second condition (the place) into the act, a pitfall the card names, and writing the log is near-daily anyway, so most of us will press 5 whatever the founder's range.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, on how many days did you still have the day's photos and notes to put into the daily log after your walks? 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 · 5 · I can't recall

screens.why1: Right after asking how often I wrote my log in the trailer, it makes sense to ask how that chore stacks up against the rest of my day.
screens.why2: RFIs, submittals and subs are everyday words on my jobs, so I can answer on the first read.
screens.why3: I deal with every one of these on a normal day as super, so I know which one I'd want eased.
screens.why4: Keeping the job on schedule is nearly my whole job, and it holds getting subs to show up and finish, which is one of the main reasons a job slips, so those two overlap.
screens.why5: Logging the day's photos and notes is the chore the study is about, in words I'd use, and nothing about anybody's product comes through.
screens.why6: Five short options, easy to hold when heard once, and R-F-Is says fine out loud to anyone in the trade.
screens.why7: The own row is there and not first, and the escape is at the first ask, but one rule is bent: the schedule row swallows the subs row and is close to the whole job, and the RFIs row joins two things.
screens.instead: Think of your last day on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Chasing RFIs · Keeping the lookahead current · Logging the day's photos and notes · Running the safety walk · Getting subs to show up and finish · None of these

screens.why1: After asking what I'd most like made easier, asking how my last log went is the obvious next question for a super who writes the log every day.
screens.why2: 'Uploading photos' is plain to me, but then the answers talk about when and where the log got done, so I'd read it twice to work out which I'm answering.
screens.why3: I upload the day's photos to Procore and write the log myself, so I know exactly how my last one went.
screens.why4: The question asks how the photo upload went, but the answers are about where and when the log was finished, so my true answer ('the upload took most of an hour and timed out twice') isn't there; 'at home or the next morning' joins two answers, and 'I can't recall' doesn't fit when the assistant super or project engineer often does the uploading.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but the founder's act of getting the photos and notes into the log has shrunk to the photo upload alone in the question and drifted to when the log was done in the answers.
screens.why6: Heard once it's short and the five answers say well as a list, even if what they answer doesn't match the question.
screens.why7: The answers are not on one measure: place (on site, at home), time (under an hour, a couple of hours) and quality (not written up properly) are mixed, a stand-in for the cost; they answer a different act than the question asks ('at home or the next morning' is a joined rung); and the escape should be 'Someone else did it', since the uploading is often handed off, not 'I can't recall'.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did getting the day's photos and notes into it take? Under 15 minutes; 15 to 30 minutes; about an hour; two hours or more; or it didn't get done that day. Or say someone else did it.
